messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Control-plane dependency errors — elevated 5xx and timeouts observed across auth and org-lookup. Impact: user requests returning 502/504 from gateway. Pager: @alice oncall. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/control-plane-deps

alice: oncall here, got the page. seeing spike in 502/504 from gateway -> control-plane. grafana shows auth latency and org-lookup timeouts spiking at 02:03 UTC. tagging dmitri to assist.

dmitri: on it. quick check of auth pods — increased error rate and redis timeouts. `redis-cluster` for auth has high 99th latency. also seeing `503` from `org-lookup` service downstream. attaching a few logs.

alice: copying logs to thread, pasting top errors:
```
ERROR auth: upstream timeout=5000ms conn=pool-3 host=redis-auth-1:6379
WARN org-lookup: service timeout while calling billing-lookup
HTTP 502 from control-plane/proxy -> backend auth-service (connection reset)
```

dmitri: running quick probes:
```
kubectl -n control-plane exec -it auth-pod-0 -- redis-cli --latency -h redis-auth-1
kubectl -n control-plane logs deploy/auth-service | grep "timeout" | tail -n 20
```

ben: I can flip the standby auth pool and divert traffic to `auth-standby-v2` (no schema change). will do a controlled failover under `auth-failover` runbook. prepping command.

li: i'm going to temporarily relax org-lookup rate limits in the config-service to reduce pressure and give redis time to recover. patching config: `POST /internal/config/limits` (will annotate change).

support-bot: Current impact estimate: ~12-18% of API requests failing intermittently. Top affected customers: [Acme Corp, Skylab], a few mobile clients on older SDKs.

chris: FYI product — any active sync jobs that will be especially sensitive? we should notify CS if SLAs likely missed.

alice: declaring incident P1 due to customer-facing 5xx spike. notifying CSE. ben, proceed with failover and post-step verification.

ben: executing failover now, running health checks after switch.

ben: failover done. `auth-standby-v2` is receiving traffic. health check summary:
```
200 OK /health (auth-standby-v2) x4 checks
avg latency down to 60ms from 1.2s
5xx count down ~78% in last 5m
```

dmitri: redis cluster still showing degraded latency on shard A; working with infra to rotate pods. but failover reduced client-facing errors immediately.

li: rate-limit relax applied, config change id `cfg-8342`, propagating. also enabling additional caching for org-lookup keys for 10m TTL.

alice: quick customer impact note: Gateway errors reduced significantly post-failover. dashboards show 5xx rate back to near baseline for most regions, but EU edge still has intermittent 504s (followup).

support-bot: Notifying top affected customers via CSE template: `INCIDENT: temporary errors, mitigation in place. follow-up postmortem to come.`

alice: handing on-call to dmitri for RCA and follow-up, I need to step away in 25m. dmitri take lead. :white_check_mark: @dmitri

dmitri: taking lead. plan: 1) stabilize redis cluster (rotate pods, check connections) 2) investigate root cause for spike (deploy, client behavior) 3) schedule postmortem. I'll create an incident ticket in Jira (RED-INC-2028) and link runbook notes.

chris: please include timeline and customer impact numbers in the ticket so PM/CS can prepare comms.

alice: thanks all. follow-up actions assigned in the incident ticket. leaving this channel for now. :zap:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (auth failover + rate-limit relax). 5xx reduced by ~78% system-wide. Next update from dmitri in ~30m or on significant changes.
